judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's readings are correct and I checked each against the rendered page. Graph A is a pgfplots bar chart on a 0-12 axis ticked by twos with Ana 8, Ben 6, Cruz 12, Dee 4, so problem 3's difference is 8 and problem 4's maximum is 12. Graph B's line plot draws 4:2, 5:4, 6:3, 7:1, so four boxes held 5 pencils and the mode is 5. Problem 7's four figures are a triangle, a rectangle, a pentagon and a hexagon (3, 4, 5, 6 sides), so Theo's 'C: 6, D: 5' really is the swap and shape C has five sides. Item 8 is correctly typed manual with a rubric that names both acceptable drawings and acceptable sentences. Two findings the judge did not reach. First, problem 2 asks two questions in one stem — 'What is one step really worth, and how many books did Ben read?' — and verify.json id 2 has a single entry, expected 6. The scale value 2 is the entire point of the item (it is the misconception the sheet is built around, and the header instruction tells the child to find it first), yet nothing verifies it and the Quick Answers bank prints only '2. 6'. Second, on print quality at 4/4: Graph A and Graph B are printed once, in the preamble of page 1, and are used by problems 2 through 6 on pages 2 and 3, so a seven-year-old must flip back and forth for five of the eight problems. The sibling cases in this batch, curr-096 and curr-097, reprint the figure beside every problem that reads it — the same author system solved this problem two cases earlier.

strengths_to_preserve: The two-per-step scale is not decoration: every one of problems 1-4 declares a trap whose value is the step-count misreading (4, 3, 4 and 6 against the correct 8, 6, 8 and 12), so the sheet is diagnostic by construction rather than by luck — a wrong answer names the exact misconception in the key's 'Common wrong answers' block.

Problem 6 warns the child about the very confusion it tests ('the answer is the number written under the tallest stack, not how many marks are in it') and still declares the trap value 4 for the child who answers with the stack height. Warning and trap together is the right treatment for a mode question on a line plot.

Problem 7's four figures are drawn with 3, 4, 5 and 6 straight sides so the claimed swap is verifiable by counting rather than by recognising shape names, which keeps the item inside the grade band while still exercising attribute reasoning.

Item 8 is correctly declared manual, takes no answer line (the drawing is the answer), gives the child a grid to draw on, and its desc lists several acceptable drawings AND the two shapes of acceptable sentence, so two graders would mark it the same way.

The study guide's Skill 1 teaches the scale rule generically rather than for this one graph — it shows both a step of 2 and a step of 5, then states 'steps in the bar x what one step is worth = the amount' — and its watch-out is the sheet's thesis in one line: 'Counting the steps is not the answer. It is only half of it.'

root_causes.description: A stem asking two questions carries one verify entry, because nothing compares printed answer slots with covered entries. Here the unchecked value is not incidental — it is the scale factor the whole sheet is about.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 2: 'Nia forgot to look at the numbers up the side. What is one step really worth, and how many books did Ben read?'

verify.json id 2: one entry, {"type": "read_data", "query": "value", "key": "Ben", "expected": 6}. The step value 2 appears in the trap desc ('where each step is worth two') but never as a checked answer.

answer_key.pdf Quick Answers prints '2. 6'; the key's body does supply the other half ('The numbers up the side go 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, so each step is worth 2 books, not 1'), so the grader is served and the verification record is not.
The sheet's own header instruction makes the step value a required first answer: 'Find two numbers that are next to each other on the side to see what one step is worth.'

root_causes.description: A figure shared by several problems is emitted once in the document preamble, so problems that depend on it can land pages away from it. tests/check_layout.py's figure-scope rule is designed for the opposite hazard (a figure-less problem sitting beside one whose figure carries data) and does not fire when the data-bearing figure lives outside every problem region, so a multi-page sheet can separate a question from the graph it reads with no gate objecting.
evidence: worksheet.tex emits both charts before problem 1, in the sheet's introductory block, captioned 'Graph A ... Use it for problems 1 to 4' and 'Graph B ... Use it for problems 5 and 6'.

worksheet.pdf pagination: Graph A and Graph B are on page 1 with problem 1; problems 2, 3, 4 and 5 are on page 2; problem 6 is on page 3. Five of the eight problems read a figure that is not on their page.

curr-096 (same batch, same author system) repeats its picture graph inside problems 1, 2, 3, 7 and 8 and its bar chart inside problems 4, 5 and 6; curr-097 repeats its line plots beside every problem. Both scored 4/4 on the same dimension without the flip.
tests/check_layout.py's figure-scope rule keys on regions with a valued figure ('has_valued_figure(r)'); here no problem region holds one, so the rule is vacuous.

improvements.title: Count printed answer slots per problem and require one covered verify entry for each
improvements.proposed_change: Extend tests/check_answer_line.py (already receives the worksheet .tex and verify.json, already build.sh gate 10) to count \ansblank / \ansline / \answerline per segmented problem region — plus the one line \problem emits when its workspace argument is positive — and compare with the number of verify entries for that id carrying an 'expected' value or "type": "manual". Exit 1 on an undercount naming the problem and both counts. For curr-099 the fix is one entry under id 2 recording the scale value 2 (an eval over the axis step, or a read_data query over the same data dict), so the sheet's central quantity is proved rather than merely mentioned inside a trap description.
improvements.regression_test: Add tests/fixtures/slot_undercount_scale/ with a worksheet problem reading 'What is one step really worth,~\ansblank and how many books did Ben read?~\ansblank' against a verify.json id-1 holding one read_data entry (expected 6). Assert check_answer_line.py exits 1 reporting '2 printed answer slots, 1 covered'; add an entry for the step value 2 and assert exit 0.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the run's largest verification gap (61 cases). On this sheet it forces the scale factor — the one number the entire worksheet is about — into the verification record and into the Quick Answers bank, where a grader will actually see it.
improvements.risk: Authors may respond by deleting scaffold blanks rather than declaring their values, which would make early-elementary sheets worse. The failure message must lead with 'declare the value' and offer 'merge the lines' second, and SKILL.md should state that scaffold blanks are encouraged provided their answers are recorded.

improvements.title: A figure a problem must read has to be on that problem's page
improvements.proposed_change: State the rule in SKILL.md's layout section and in references/latex-templates.md: a data-bearing figure referenced by more than one problem is emitted inside EACH problem region that reads it (as curr-096 and curr-097 do by repeating the tikzpicture), or, when the figure is too large to repeat, the sheet declares a figure page and the dependent problems are kept on the facing page. Back it with a check in tests/check_layout.py: when a problem region names a figure by label ('Graph A', 'the finished plot', 'the same line plot') and no valued figure appears in that region, warn; escalate to a failure when the compiled page number of the region differs from the page carrying the figure, which the driver can determine from the same engine log that the compile-ws gate already reads for the page count.
improvements.regression_test: Add tests/fixtures/offpage_shared_figure/ with a two-page worksheet whose bar chart is emitted in the preamble on page 1 and whose problem 3 on page 2 reads 'Graph A. How many more books did Cruz read than Dee?' with no figure in its own region. Assert the extended check_layout.py exits 1 naming problem 3 and the page gap; move a copy of the tikzpicture into problem 3's region and assert exit 0.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes a real handling burden for seven-to-nine-year-olds on exactly the sheets most likely to need one — graph reading, where every question depends on a picture. Two other cases in this same batch already do it right, so the fix is codifying existing good practice rather than inventing it.
improvements.risk: Repeating a large figure inflates page count, and the sheet is already page-budgeted (scripts/page_budget.py). For a big chart the right answer is the facing-page layout rather than repetition, so the check must offer both remedies or it will trade a flipping problem for a page-bloat problem. Determining a region's compiled page number reliably is the implementation hazard; start the rule as a warning and promote it once the page mapping is proven.

case_summary: A well-aimed error-analysis sheet: every value checks out (Graph A at 8, 6, 12, 4 on a two-per-step axis; Graph B at 4:2, 5:4, 6:3, 7:1; shapes with 3, 4, 5 and 6 sides so Theo's C/D swap is real), seven traps are declared and each lands on a different number from the correct answer, and item 8 is properly declared manual with a rubric covering both the drawing and the sentence. The study guide teaches the scale rule generically rather than for this one chart. Two defects sit under the 32/32. Problem 2 asks two questions — what one step is worth, and how many books Ben read — and verify.json records only the second; the step value of 2 is the misconception the entire sheet is built around, and it survives only inside a trap description and the key's prose. And both graphs are printed once, in the page-1 preamble, while problems 2 through 6 that read them sit on pages 2 and 3, so five of eight problems make a young child flip pages; curr-096 and curr-097 in this same batch repeat their figures beside every problem that uses them and scored the same 4/4 on visual and print quality. Neither defect requires a number to change.
